records.finding: The original PP13B report puts food shells in LC-MSA Lower at roughly 164 ± 12 ka, with brown mussel the most abundant taxon by minimum number of individuals. It infers accessible rocky shores and tidal pools from habitat. The existing press-release event was the same observation and is consolidated into the bounded excavation event. Bajondillo is a roughly contemporaneous comparison, so worldwide priority is left open. Shells and flaked tools in the same stratum do not show that a named technique supplied shellfish procurement.

records.next: Inspect shell growth increments, assemblage taphonomy and any object with securely identified contact wear in the oldest dated PP13B subcontext. Such evidence could refine collecting conditions or a tool relationship.

records.finding: Jerimalai's oldest Square B assemblage includes scombrids, identified at family level in 2011. Independent comparative habitat data leave either inshore or offshore capture possible. The later shell hook in Square A, spit 29, and the dated Alor burial hook remain separate observations. Shared types across Wallacea and later Pacific fishing do not date the early capture technique or prove a specific transmission route.

records.finding: The excavation documents a discrete fish-rich gutter. Later strontium evidence distinguishes sampled fish in and out of the pit, and the authors infer autumn roach gathering. That season is inferred from ecology; the isotope tests address provenance rather than fermentation. The Antrea net is a comparison with separate chronology and geography, and does not identify Norje gear or imply transfer. The baseline scope and site date are retained.

records.finding: Early Phase 2 mound bases represent a separate land-preparation achievement. Denham, Golson and Hughes interpret banana phytolith concentrations in the adjacent feature fills as deliberate planting in those mounded plots. Excavated field architecture and plant residues are distinct kinds of evidence. Their spatial attribution is an inference from fills and the studies overlap in authors and material, so the local uses_process relation stays a candidate. The westward dispersal discussed by Perrier and colleagues combines regional genetics and linguistics; neither traces a specific plant line directly out of the sampled Kuk plots.

records.finding: The museum attributes food residues to its Cuddie Springs grindstone; its reported age depends on context. Field, Fullagar and Lord argue for preservation of the Pleistocene sediments, while independent ESR/U-series work on fauna complicates the association of remains and sediments. The Madjedbebe seed processing interpretation uses wear and organic residues on different objects from a different context; it supplies a comparison but no lineage.

records.finding: Hiscock and colleagues report a single diagnostic fragment with associated charcoal in CG1 A2 excavation unit 52. The later site synthesis's table includes the same Wk-37976 determination, so it is not a second date for the fragment. The more ancient reported evidence from Madjedbebe is a separate Australian site. Similarity and chronology alone leave routes and continuity unresolved. The baseline record is retained.
